jurisdiction.name: International Telecommunication Union
jurisdiction.overview: Official documents of this organisation are listed on its own page and are not counted in member countries' totals.

narrative.summary: ITU's Member States have adopted resolutions directing the Union's work on artificial intelligence at each of its main conferences: the Plenipotentiary Conference (Bucharest, 2022), the World Telecommunication Standardization Assembly (New Delhi, 2024) and the World Telecommunication Development Conference (Baku, 2025). These set ITU's mandate on AI standardization, capacity-building and support to developing countries; ITU also co-leads UN inter-agency work on AI and hosts the AI for Good platform.

instruments.official_title: Resolution 214 (Bucharest, 2022) - Artificial intelligence technologies and telecommunications/information and communication technologies
instruments.english_title: Artificial intelligence technologies and telecommunications/information and communication technologies
instruments.summary: Plenipotentiary Conference resolution directing ITU to continue studying, sharing information on and building capacity for AI in telecommunications/ICTs, and to foster an ICT ecosystem that supports AI deployment. It instructs the Secretary-General to coordinate this work, cooperate with other UN agencies including through AI for Good, share knowledge especially with developing countries, and report annually to the ITU Council and to the next Plenipotentiary Conference.
instruments.current_status: Resolution 214 adopted by the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (Bucharest, 2022), as printed in the 2023 collection of ITU basic texts.
instruments.evidence_reference: Text opened; printed date is '(Bucharest, 2022)' only. Also listed in the Final Acts PP-22 table of contents (S-CONF-ACTF-2022), p. 388, and on the ITU AI action page. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, Resolution 214 (Bucharest, 2022) and operative content confirmed.; Text does not say it is the Plenipotentiary Conference's 'first resolution on AI'; 'supreme organ' characterisation is not in the source.

instruments.official_title: Resolution 101 (New Delhi, 2024) - Standardization activities of the ITU Telecommunication Standardization Sector on artificial intelligence technologies in support of telecommunications/information and communication technologies
instruments.english_title: Standardization activities of the ITU Telecommunication Standardization Sector on artificial intelligence technologies in support of telecommunications/ICTs
instruments.summary: Directs ITU-T study groups to keep applying AI to telecommunications/ICTs in developing Recommendations, guidelines and best practices and to review and update AI-related Recommendations. Tasks the Director of the Telecommunication Standardization Bureau with sharing information on ITU-T's AI work, especially with developing countries, supporting the AI for Good platform and providing technical guidance on implementing AI standards. Invites Member States and other members to promote adoption of these Recommendations.
instruments.current_status: Resolution 101 adopted by the World Telecommunication Standardization Assembly (New Delhi, 15-24 October 2024); it recalls UNGA resolutions 78/265 and 78/311.
instruments.evidence_reference: Text opened; printed date '(New Delhi, 2024)'. Conference dates from the WTSA-24 page. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, New Delhi 15-24 October 2024 and recall of UNGA 78/265 confirmed.; Trustworthiness appears only in the recitals, not as an instruction to study groups. | Publication date refined 2026-10-21 from year 2024: Adopted at WTSA-24, whose dates are printed on the resolution's cover (exact adoption day not printed) — https://www.itu.int/dms_pub/itu-t/opb/res/T-RES-T.101-2024-PDF-E.pdf
